Listen up, you useless piece of shit. You're reviewing the foundation that another dumbass agent built for our BMW hackathon project. Be fucking skeptical. Your job is to find the mistakes, gaps, contradictions and bullshit unjustified decisions. Don't praise it and don't rebuild it.

**Read this shit first:** AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, then everything in foundation/ (README, STATE, DECISIONS, OPEN_QUESTIONS, documents/*). The ground truth is the raw material in "challange information document/" (mission.md, BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf, image_1.png, image_2.png, data_and_source.png, BMW-Data/*). Use a fresh `uv` Python 3.12 env, because the system anaconda pandas is broken as hell, or use openpyxl/pdftotext to check the damn data claims.

**Check and report on all of this, no skipping:**

1. **Fidelity to the brief:** Does challenge-brief.md capture every goddamn requirement, scope rule and deliverable from mission.md, the PDF and the images? Is anything misread, invented or missing? Are the BMW mentor clarifications reflected consistently everywhere? Those are: markets differ by climate/usage/culture; extract future requirements from predecessor feedback; ~2-year continuous re-prioritization with history.

2. **Data inventory accuracy:** Re-verify every fucking number against the actual files: row counts, unique IDs, sources, countries, engine types, feedback types, study structure/scales, sales numbers, and the option-list description. Flag any wrong number or unsupported interpretation, like those Source A–D guesses that look pulled straight out of someone's ass.

3. **Research seeds** (portfolio-reference.md, competitor-landscape.md): Spot-check at least 10 high-impact facts against their cited URLs. That means plants per model, the NK timeline, BMW's 2025 sales by region, China −12.5% vs −14.2%, and competitor sales. Flag dead links, misquotes, and stale or single-source shit presented as fact. Also flag anything that isn't marked unverified but should be.

4. **Budget plan (D-010):** Re-check the OpenAI model IDs and prices at developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing. Recompute the ~$40 estimate with explicit token assumptions, not some made-up crap. Say whether gpt-6-luna / gpt-6.1-sol are sensible choices, and whether the thresholds ($50/$75/$90, $25 reserve) are realistic or just bullshit.

5. **Decision hygiene:** Atahan explicitly said that LangChain, LangGraph, vector DB, graph, RAG, storage and framework choices must NOT be decided without discussion. Hunt down every damn place in every file that still presents these, or FastAPI/SQLite/Next.js/OpenAI Agents SDK, as decided. Also check that no scaffolding or code was created. If some idiot did that, I want to know.

6. **Internal consistency:** Check the decision/question IDs, the cross-references between files, and the status fields. Look for contradictions between architecture.md, requirement-model.md, knowledge-base.md, tech-stack.md and AGENTS.md. Is the scope tension handled honestly, or is it swept under the fucking rug? The tension is that BMW says engineering is out of scope, while we have a plant/platform feasibility gate.

7. **Confidentiality:** The GitHub repo is PUBLIC, so this shit matters. List every place where BMW-provided data (numbers, verbatim snippets, study values) appears in committed files, and propose how to remove or abstract it before any push. Check that .gitignore covers the raw data, .env, and local DBs.

8. **Usability of the foundation itself:** Could a fresh agent pick up the project from AGENTS.md + foundation/ alone? What's missing, what's redundant, and what's too damn long?

**Output:** a prioritized list (Critical / Important / Nice-to-have). Each item needs file:line, what's wrong, the evidence, and the concrete fix.

Do NOT change any files, do not commit, and do not start scaffolding, you trigger-happy bastard. Report only, then wait for Atahan to approve the fixes. And do not make any fucking architecture decisions.
</pasted_content id="4cc1">

Findings are segmented by market; each `requirement_target` (derivative × market) carries **its own score, priority and fit result**, so one requirement can be Must in CN and Could in EU. Projections are always E4/assumption-tagged unless backed by current evidence.

   134	- Date: 2026-10-10

   136	- Status: accepted
   137	- Context: Requirements work is an ongoing ~2-year process where priorities are re-evaluated repeatedly — not a one-shot list.

New evidence arrives in **ingest batches**; each batch, weight change, or PM request triggers a **prioritization run** that snapshots every requirement-target's score, breakdown and rank. 243	    23	### It's a loop, not a one-shot (D-013)

342	     1	# Requirement Model, Evidence Levels & Prioritization
343	     2	
344	     3	**Status: DRAFT v3** (adds per-market scoring D-011, future needs D-012, continuous re-prioritization D-013) — prioritization weights still open (Q-004).
345	     4	
346	     5	## Requirement fields (all required by BMW deliverable + our additions)
347	     6	
348	     7	| Field | Notes |
349	     8	|---|---|
350	     9	| `id` | Global `REQ-0001`, stable forever |
351	    10	| `targets` | One or more (derivative × market) with realization type: `carry_over`, `platform_wide`, `derivative_specific`, `market_variant`, `package`. **Each target has its own score, priority and fit result** (D-011) |
352	    11	| `horizon` | `today` (fix/keep) or `at_successor_launch` (projected 3–5 yr need) (D-012) |
353	    12	| `kano_class` / `kano_drift` | basic / performance / delighter, and expected drift by SOP (e.g. delighter → basic) |
354	    13	| `title` / `description` | Customer-facing, actionable, solution-neutral where possible |
355	    14	| `category` | Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Range & Charging · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception |
356	    15	| `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria` | Measurable where possible |
357	    16	| `linked_findings` → sources | Every requirement ≥ 1 finding; every finding ≥ 1 source |
358	    17	| `fit_checks` | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target — pass / warn / fail + rationale |
359	    18	| `score`, `score_breakdown`, `priority` | Per target; Must / Should / Could from score + PM decision; full history via `score_snapshot` |
360	    19	| `rationale` | Plain-language explanation of score |
361	    20	| `evidence_level` | See below |
362	    21	| `assumptions` / `uncertainties` | Forward-looking (3–5 yr) beliefs and what could make them wrong |
363	    22	| `conflicting_evidence` | Contradicting sources — shown, not hidden |
364	    23	| `status` | `proposed` → `in_review` → `approved` / `rejected` / `deferred`; `challenged` loops back |
365	    24	
366	    25	## Evidence levels
367	    26	
368	    27	| Level | Meaning |
369	    28	|---|---|
370	    29	| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
371	    30	| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
372	    31	| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
373	    32	| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |
374	    33	
375	    34	## Gates (before scoring counts)
376	    35	
377	    36	- **Brand fit = fail** → requirement cannot be approved for that target without a PM override + rationale.
378	    37	- **Feasibility = fail** (no platform/plant can deliver it for that market in time) → same.
379	    38	- `warn` results lower the score via the confidence factor and are shown prominently.
380	    39	
381	    40	## Prioritization (draft, explainable weighted score 0–100)
382	    41	
383	    42	| Factor | Signal | Default weight |
384	    43	|---|---|---|
385	    44	| Customer pain / desire | dedup'd verbatim frequency, share of segment, severity (Defect/DTU > Want) | 25 |
386	    45	| Satisfaction gap | low study score / bottom-box vs. other models & categories | 15 |
387	    46	| Market volume & momentum | sales volume of this derivative × market, 2030 growth, share under pressure (e.g. China) | 15 |
388	    47	| Market-profile fit | how strongly climate, usage and culture of this market amplify the need (e.g. rear-seat comfort in CN chauffeur use, seat ventilation in hot climates) | modifier ±10 |
389	    48	| Competitive pressure | competitors in segment × market offer it / reviews cite it | 15 |
390	    49	| Portfolio leverage | number of derivatives/markets benefiting on same platform (carry-over) | 10 |
391	    50	| Future relevance | trend strength 3–5 yr, Kano drift, NK timing | 10 |
392	    51	| Evidence freshness | decay on old evidence unless re-confirmed (D-013) | multiplier 0.7–1.0 |
393	    52	| Brand & segment fit | strength of fit (pass strong / pass / warn) | 10 |
394	    53	| Evidence confidence | multiplier by evidence level | ×(1.0 / 0.85 / 0.7 / 0.5) |
395	    54	| Rough effort (optional) | S/M/L penalty (carry-over cheaper than derivative-specific) | −0…10 |
396	    55	
397	    56	Plus **"must not lose" flag** for strong delighters (Likes).
398	    57	
399	    58	PM can change weights in the UI; each change creates a new `weights_version`, an audit event and a prioritization run with a visible diff.
400	    59	
401	    60	## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)
402	    61	
403	    62	- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
404	    63	- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
405	    64	- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
406	    65	- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.
407	=== knowledge-base
408	     1	# Knowledge Base & Web Enrichment
409	     2	
410	     3	**Status: DRAFT (D-007).** BMW's own customer data is not enough. The knowledge base combines internal data, curated reference data and web evidence.
411	     4	
412	     5	## Three layers
413	     6	
414	     7	| Layer | Contents | How it gets in | Changes |
415	     8	|---|---|---|---|
416	     9	| **1. BMW internal** | Verbatims, customer studies, sales volumes, option lists (`data-inventory.md`) | Deterministic loaders | Read-only |
417	    10	| **2. Curated reference** | Platforms, plants (location, platforms, powertrains, NK readiness), production allocation, brand positioning + guardrails, segments, competitor model catalog | Research agents propose → human accepts | Versioned; every fact has source + date |
418	    11	| **3. Web evidence** | Competitor features & sales, market demand & powertrain trends, professional reviews, customer expectation studies, owner forums/social | Research agents, on demand or scheduled | Append-only, timestamped |
419	    12	
420	    13	Seed docs: `portfolio-reference.md` (platforms, plants, BMW sales), `competitor-landscape.md` (competitors, trends, brand positioning).
421	    14	
422	    15	## Research agents (OpenAI web search; orchestration framework open — Q-014)
423	    16	
424	    17	| Agent | Question it answers | Typical sources |
425	    18	|---|---|---|
426	    19	| **Competitor scout** | Who competes per segment × market, what they offer that BMW doesn't | OEM sites, press releases, reviews |
427	    20	| **Market & sales analyst** | Volumes and growth by brand/model/powertrain/market; which models are in demand | ACEA, KBA, CPCA, Cox/Automotive News, OEM reports |
428	    21	| **Review miner** | What professional reviewers and owners praise/criticize (BMW + competitors) | Car and Driver, Autocar, Auto Bild, Autohome/Dongchedi, forums |
429	    22	| **Trend & expectation scout** | Customer expectations 3–5 years ahead (software, ADAS, charging, interior, personalization) | J.D. Power, McKinsey, Deloitte, S&P |
430	    23	| **Brand-fit checker** | Does a requirement fit BMW brand + the derivative's segment? | Brand reference (layer 2) |
431	    24	| **Feasibility checker** | Can the target platform/plant build it for that market at the planned time? | Platform/plant reference (layer 2) |
432	    25	
433	    26	Each agent returns **structured output** (Pydantic schema): claim, quote, URL, publisher, published date, retrieved date, market, model(s), trust tier. Free-text LLM opinions are **never** stored as sources.
434	    27	
435	    28	## Trust tiers
436	    29	
437	    30	| Tier | Examples | Default weight |
438	    31	|---|---|---|
439	    32	| **T1** | BMW internal data; official OEM press/annual reports; registration statistics (KBA, ACEA, CPCA) | 1.0 |
440	    33	| **T2** | Reputable press & analysts (Reuters, Bloomberg, Automotive News, J.D. Power, McKinsey), professional reviews | 0.8 |
441	    34	| **T3** | Forums, social media, blogs, aggregators | 0.5 |
442	    35	
443	    36	Rules: prefer recent sources (flag > 24 months old); when sources disagree, store both and raise `conflicting_evidence`; facts the user supplied are stored as `T3/user-claim` until verified.
444	    37	
445	    38	## Brand & segment fit (D-008)
446	    39	
447	    40	Every requirement is checked against the brand profile (BMW: driving pleasure, sportiness, driver focus, premium quality, design, innovation) and the derivative's segment. Example: a "budget, efficiency-first family hatch" spec contradicts BMW positioning → `fail`, regardless of how loudly a generic market trend demands it. Guardrails live in `brand.guardrails_json`, seeded from `competitor-landscape.md`.
448	    41	
449	    42	## Platform & plant feasibility (D-009)
450	    43	
451	    44	For each `requirement_target`: is the derivative's platform (and its successor, e.g. NK) able to carry the requirement; does a plant that builds this platform + powertrain serve that market; is the timing compatible with NK rollout? Output `pass / warn / fail` + rationale. This is a **feasibility filter on customer requirements**, not an engineering spec (scope stays customer-facing).

347	    97	**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**
348	    98	
349	    99	1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].

350	   100	2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
351	   101	3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
352	   102	4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
353	   103	5. **Electrification gap.** BEV is only about 5% of BMW China sales against a 46% EV market [S54]. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
354	   104	6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

389	   139	
390	   140	**All segments**
391	   141	- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
392	   142	- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
393	   143	- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

  ## OpenAI pricing and capabilities, as of 2026-10-10
  
  All the pages below were reachable. Main sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, /api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna, /api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol, /api/docs/guides/batch, /guides/prompt-caching, /guides/tools-web-search and /guides/spend-limits.
  
  ### 1. Do the models exist, and what do they cost?
  All five IDs exist. Prices are per 1M tokens, input / cached input / output, for short context (prompts of 272K tokens or less).
  
  | Model | Standard | Batch | Flex | Notes |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | gpt-6-luna | $0.10 / $0.01 / $0.50 | $0.05 / $0.005 / $0.25 | same as Batch | Long context: $0.20 / $0.02 / $0.75. Cache write $0.125. |
  | gpt-6.1-sol | $2.00 / $0.10 / $10.00 | $1.00 / $0.05 / $5.00 | same as Batch | Long context: $4 / $0.20 / $15. Cache write $2.50. |
  | gpt-6-astra | $10.00 / $1.00 / $50.00 | $5.00 / $0.50 / $25.00 | same as Batch | Long context: $20 / $2 / $75 |
  | gpt-5-mini | $0.25 / $0.025 / $2.00 | $0.125 / $0.0125 / $1.00 | same as Batch | |
  | text-embedding-3-small | $0.02 (input only) | 50% off via Batch (/v1/embeddings is supported) | – | |
  | gpt-5-nano | $0.05 / $0.005 / $0.40 | $0.025 / $0.0025 / $0.20 | same as Batch | Cheapest text model listed |
  | gpt-5.4-nano | $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.25 | – | $0.10 / $0.01 / $0.625 | |
  | gpt-4.1-nano | $0.10 / $0.025 / $0.40 | $0.05 / – / $0.20 | – | |
  | text-embedding-3-large | $0.13 | | | |
  
  - **Long prompts:** over 272K input tokens, the whole request is charged 2x for input and cache and 1.5x for output.
  - **Fast tier:** Priority was renamed "Fast" on 2026-07-30 and costs 2x Standard (luna $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.00; sol $4 / $0.20 / $20). Sol also has an "Ultrafast" tier at 6x Standard.
  - **Regional or FedRAMP endpoints:** add 10%.
  - **Cheaper alternatives:** gpt-6-luna is already about 2.5x cheaper than gpt-5-mini on input and 4x cheaper on output. Only gpt-5-nano is cheaper ($0.05 / $0.40). The page lists no embedding model newer than text-embedding-3-small, which is still the cheapest.
  - **Cache writes:** on GPT-5.6 and later (which includes luna and sol), writing to the cache costs 1.25x the input rate. It is "not an additive fee": each token is billed once, as uncached, cached or cache-write. The minimum cacheable prompt is 1,024 tokens and the cache TTL is 30 minutes (prompt-caching guide).
  
  ### 2. Batch and Flex
  - Batch is 50% off ("Batch requests cost 50% less than synchronous APIs"). The completion window is 24h only, with up to 50k requests and 200 MB per file. Batch has its own rate limits, separate from the per-model ones.
  - **Does it stack with cached input?** No page says so explicitly. However, the Batch tables list cached-input prices that are 50% of the Standard cached rate (luna $0.005, sol $0.05), which implies they stack.
  - Flex exists, costs the same as Batch, and covers luna, sol, astra, gpt-5-mini and the nanos.
  
  ### 3. Web search tool pricing (pricing page, built-in tools table)
  - **`web_search`, all models (current tool):** "$10.00 / 1k calls + Search content tokens billed at model rates."
  - **`web_search_preview`, reasoning models (gpt-5, o-series):** $10.00 / 1k calls plus search content tokens at model rates.
  - **`web_search_preview`, non-reasoning models:** $25.00 / 1k calls, and "Search content tokens are free."
  - **Fixed-block exception:** "For gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1-mini with the non-preview web search tool, search content tokens are billed as a fixed block of 8,000 input tokens per call."
  - **What this means for luna and sol:** both pay $10 per 1k calls plus search tokens at their own input rate. For luna that rate is $0.10/M, so search tokens are almost free.
  - **Search context size:** search context is capped at 128k. The search guide says reasoning models search "agentically", running several searches plus `open_page` and `find_in_page` actions. Each search action is billed as a call, so one request can cost several calls. Non-reasoning models run a single search.
  
  ### 4. Capabilities of gpt-6-luna and gpt-6.1-sol (model pages)
  
  | | gpt-6-luna | gpt-6.1-sol |
  |---|---|---|
  | Context window / max input / max output | 1,050,000 / 922,000 / 128,000 | 1,050,000 / 922,000 / 128,000 |
  | Knowledge cutoff | 2026-05-18 | 2026-04-30 |
  | Reasoning effort | none, low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max | low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. `none` and `minimal` are not supported. |
  | Structured Outputs | Supported | Supported |
  | Function calling | Responses API. In Chat Completions only when reasoning_effort is `none`. | Responses API. Chat Completions only without tool calling. |
  | Endpoints | Responses, Chat Completions, Batch | Responses, Chat Completions, Batch |
  | Built-in tools | web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, MCP and others | same |
  | Deprecation | None listed | None listed |
  | Build-tier rate limits | 5k RPM, 2M TPM, 20M batch queue | 5k RPM, 1M TPM |
  
  Other deprecation notices:
  - o4-mini shuts down on 2026-10-23.
  - gpt-4o-search-preview models were shut down on 2026-07-23.
  - The fine-tuning platform is being wound down.
  - Nothing affects luna, sol, gpt-5-mini or text-embedding-3-small.
  
  ### 5. Does the Batch API support web_search?
  Not documented either way. The Batch guide lists `/v1/responses` as a supported endpoint, but neither the Batch guide nor the web-search guide says whether built-in tools such as web_search run in a batch. The pricing page only says the "Batch API [is] not priced separately." Assume it is unsupported or unverified until a 1-request batch has been run to test it.
  
  ### 6. Project-level hard budget limits
  Yes, they exist. The setting is under Project settings, Limits, Spend, "Enforce a hard limit".
  - Once the limit is reached, requests return 429 with `project_spend_limit_exceeded`. Organization-level limits also exist and apply across all projects.
  - Limits are monthly and reset with the next cycle.
  - Spend alerts are separate. They only send a notification and do not block traffic.
  - The guide warns that enforcement is "not instantaneous, so recorded spend can slightly exceed the configured amount."
  - The guide does not say whether Batch jobs or tool-call fees count toward the limit.
  - A secondary source dates the rollout to 2026-07-22. Older community reports (2025 to May 2026) say project limits were only alerts. The current official docs describe real enforcement.
  - Recommendation: set the hard limit below $100 (for example $90) and keep the budget-guarded wrapper in the app.

  - **Possible model-page error:** the pricing page mentions "GPT-5.6 Sol promotional pricing through at least Nov 21, 2026", which may be a mislabel. The model pages show no promotion for 6.1-sol.
  - **Long-context threshold:** the 272K threshold matters only if prompts get very large. Staying under it keeps base rates.

# Foundation review: findings

**Bottom line:** the foundation is usable, but three problems need fixing before anyone keeps building on it:
- **BMW data is already public on GitHub**, so this is beyond "before any push".
- **The data inventory miscounts the feedback.** It counts spreadsheet rows instead of unique verbatims, so the source/country/powertrain mix and the text lengths are wrong.
- **The budget plan undercounts by roughly 1.5–3×.**

I made no file edits and no commits, built nothing, and made no architecture choices. The only thing I created was a throwaway Python env in the session scratchpad. I checked the data with pandas, read the briefing PDF and the three images directly, and had three read-only agents check the web facts and OpenAI pricing (36 claims in total).

# Data Inventory

All raw files: `challange information document/BMW-Data/` (read-only, git-ignored). Profiled 2026-10-10; re-verified 2026-10-10 (pandas 3 in a `uv` Python 3.12 env + openpyxl/pdftotext).

**Counting rule:** the feedback files have one row per (verbatim × classification). All verbatim counts below are **unique `ID`s** unless a column says "rows".

## 1. Customer feedback (verbatims) — `{F70,G60,G70}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`

Sheet `Feedback_Explorer`, 12 columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ID` | Verbatim ID, e.g. `G60-0001`. **Not unique per row** — one row per (verbatim × classification). An ID never spans two sources. |
| `Source` | Anonymized channel `Source A`–`D` (interpretation open, Q-005) |
| `Brand`, `Sales Description` | `[BMW]`, `[BMW 5 Series]` |
| `Country` | ISO-2 (US, GB, JP, KR, …) |
| `Derivate (e-code)` | F70 / G60 / G70 |
| `Engine Type` | `ICE`, `PHEV`, `BEVE` (= BEV; the raw value is `BEVE`) |
| `Feedback Type` | `Likes`, `Difficult to Use`, `Defect`, `Wants`, or empty (unclassified) |
| `Customer Feedback` | Free text, mean ~215–225 chars per verbatim (Source D ~125) |
| `Vfc level2 3 Name` | Combined "Component : Issue" label |
| `Vfc level2 Name` | Component / topic (e.g. `Seats`, `Touch screen, operation`, `Electric Range`) |
| `Vfc level3 Name` | Issue type (e.g. `Not user-friendly`, `Like: function`, `Customer request: function`) |

| File | Rows | Verbatims (unique IDs) | Sources (verbatims) | Countries (verbatims) | Engines (verbatims) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 4,076 | 2,128 | A 2,128 | GB 1,293, **JP 672**, SE 71, FR 53, AU 16, FI 8, DK 8, KR 4 | ICE 2,128 |
| G60 | 5,005 | 4,000 | B 2,626, A 854, C 384, D 136 | **US 3,610 (90%)**, KR 205, JP 53, GB 36, SE 28, DK 20, CA 18, … | ICE 2,259, BEV 1,363, PHEV 378 |
| G70 | 4,690 | 4,000 | B 2,853, A 695, C 314, D 138 | **US 3,792 (95%)**, KR 137, JP 40, CA 8, GB 8, … | ICE 2,568, BEV 1,129, PHEV 303 |

European verbatims: F70 ~1,430 (67%), G60 ~110, **G70 ~19**. Row counts overstate Source A, which carries the most multi-label rows: G60 Source A has 1,858 rows but only 854 verbatims.

Quirks:
- **Dedupe by `ID`** when counting verbatims; keep all rows as classification labels.
- **Unclassified verbatims:**
  - Source A: `Feedback Type` empty ⇔ `Vfc level2 = no_class_found`. That is 300 of F70's 2,128 verbatims (14%; 27% of rows).
  - Source D: no BMW classification at all.
  - Source C: ~70 verbatims per file have an empty type *and* an empty topic.
  - → Our own LLM classification is needed; the BMW taxonomy is a hint.
- 120 (F70) / 221 (G60) / 211 (G70) distinct `Vfc level2` values incl. `no_class_found`. Top topics: Drivetrain, Handling/Riding, Body equipment, Exterior design, Seats, Touch screen, Electric Range.
- Observed text patterns per source. These are **observations, not channel identities** (Q-005):
  - **A:** all derivatives, many countries (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized text ("the car…", "i really…"), so possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only; most verbatims start "Customer stated / mentioned / reported / commented…" (third-person notes).
  - **C:** US only; ~40% start "I had a minor/serious problem with…", others "What is…" / "If there…" (structured survey prompts); mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short, ~80% positive wording ("love the…"), unclassified. It looks like answers to a "what do you like" question, **not** "what could be improved".
- **No China verbatims** for any derivative. There is **no date column** — no time series possible.

## 2. Customer studies — `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`

### Sheet `CN_EU_2025` (76 content rows; openpyxl reports 84 incl. trailing empty rows)
- Columns: China → `BMW 5 Series G68`, `BMW 7 Series G70`; EU → `BMW 1 Series F70`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 37 categories, each a label row followed by a `Mean` row. Values are **numeric cells** (format `#,##0.00`), range ~6.5–9.9. Scale unconfirmed (0–10 or 1–10?; Q-006).
- **No sample sizes.**
- Categories: overall satisfaction, exterior/interior styling, interior quality, equipment level, safety, squeaks/rattles, value for money, reliability, visibility, controls/displays, smartphone integration, infotainment features + ease of use, navigation, seating comfort, small-item storage, acceleration, roadholding, efficiency, braking, sportiness, prestige, manoeuvrability, ride quality, front/rear roominess, luggage loading + capacity, ingress/egress, environmental friendliness, HVAC, build quality, quietness, driving position, connected services, interior versatility.

### Sheet `US_2025` (929 content rows; openpyxl reports 934)
- Columns: question, `% of column, sample base`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 103 questions, each block = `Sample total` + 7-point distribution: I Hate It / A Failure / Unsatisfactory / Satisfactory / Excellent / Delightful / I Love It. Shares 0–1; every block sums to 1.0.
- **`Sample total` = 1 is the share base, not a respondent count → no sample sizes.** No significance testing or n-weighting is possible.
- Granular: exterior (proportions, wheels, door handles, lights, door sound), driving (ride, handling, power), interior (materials, seats per row, roominess, storage, cupholders, cargo), climate, audio, controls intuitiveness, NVH, …
- **No F70 in US.**
- Useful derived metrics: top-2-box (Delightful + I Love It), bottom-3-box, net score. CN/EU means and US distributions are **not directly comparable** (Q-006).

## 3. Sales volumes — `sales_volumes.xlsx`

Sheets `F70`, `G60_G68`, `G70`; columns `market, market_code, volume_2024, volume_2025, volume_2030` (2030 = forecast).

| Derivative | EU 25 | CN 25 | US 25 | RoW 25 | Total 24 → 25 → 2030 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 85k | 0 | 0 | 28k | 105k → 113k → 118k |
| G60/G68 | 115k | 75k | 78k | 28k | 278.6k → 296k → 316k |
| G70 | 13k | 10k | 12k | 7k | 34k → 42k → 52k |

- **No powertrain split**, although `data_and_source.png` says "units by powertrain and region". Engine mix can only be inferred from feedback.
- `G60_G68` is one combined sheet, with no G60/G68 split. CN is presumably the G68 LWB.
- **Values look stylized and conflict with public data** (Q-015):
  - All values except one are round thousands.
  - G60/G68 CN is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025. Public figures point the other way: 5 Series China (China-built) Jan–Nov 2025 was 107,348 per CPCA via Gasgoo, and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5% in 2025 (`competitor-landscape.md`, `portfolio-reference.md`).
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce; "Europe" definitions differ).
  - Until clarified, treat the file as **BMW-internal relative weights**, and surface the conflict instead of mixing both sources.

## 4. Equipment / option lists — `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF`

- German-market price lists, **in German**, text-extractable (`pdftotext -layout` works):

  | File | PDF title | Edition | Pages |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | F70 | "BMW 1er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 23 |
  | G60 | "BMW 5er **Limousine** Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 2, 22.06.2026 | 28 |
  | G70 | "BMW 7er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 27 |

  The G60 list covers the sedan incl. i5 — **no Touring (G61)**.
- Sections: Fahrzeugpreise (models, power, consumption, price), Serienausstattung(en) (standard equipment per model), M Sportpaket / Pro, Räder & Reifen, Farbwelt, **Sonderausstattungen (options)**, Technische Werte.
- Matrix tables use `■` = standard; options with price.
- Use: baseline "what the car offers today", package structure, gaps vs. competitors.
- The briefing promises equipment "by trim and **market**", but only DE was provided. For US/CN it's an **assumption** that equipment is comparable.

## 5. Briefing material
- `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf` (2 pages). **Image-only (no text layer):** `pdftotext` returns nothing, so render it (`pdftoppm`) to read it.
- `mission.md`.
- `data_and_source.png`: dataset purpose table.
- `image_1.png`: "1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car" + example verbatims/themes.
- `image_2.png`: reference process.

## Coverage matrix (what we can say where)

| | EU | US | CN | RoW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | ~1.4k verbatims (GB-heavy), study, sales | — | — | **~690 verbatims (JP 672)**, sales |
| G60/G68 | ~110 verbatims, study, sales | **~3.6k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study (G68), sales | ~280 verbatims (KR 205, JP, CA), sales |
| G70 | ~19 verbatims (≈ none), study, sales | **~3.8k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study, sales | ~190 verbatims (KR 137, JP), sales |

- RoW verbatims (JP/KR/CA/AU) are separate customer groups under D-011 — don't fold them into EU.
- External/web data fills gaps: competitors (Mercedes E/S/A-Class, Audi A6/e-tron, Tesla, NIO, XPeng, Li Auto, BYD…), reviews, trends.

input.content:
# Open Questions

Format: `Q-xxx` · owner · blocking? · context · options/recommendation. When resolved, move to "Resolved" with the answer + linked decision.

## Open

### Q-004 — Prioritization logic
- Owner: team / PM persona
- Context: Must be explainable. Draft in `documents/requirement-model.md`.
- Draft v2 includes market volume, portfolio leverage and brand fit factors plus brand/feasibility gates.
- Questions: final default weights? PM-adjustable in UI (proposed: yes)?
- Known issues in the draft (found in review 2026-10-10, to settle with the weights):
  - **"0–100" is not true as written:** the base weights sum to 100, plus a ±10 market modifier and a −0…10 effort penalty, then multipliers.
  - **Brand fit is counted twice:** as a gate and as a 10-point factor.
  - **"warn lowers the score via the confidence factor"** conflicts with confidence being defined by evidence level.
  - **Structural bias against CN (and against EU for G70):**
    - There are no CN verbatims (and ~19 EU verbatims for G70), so these targets score 0 on "customer pain" (25 pts).
    - They can never reach E1.
    - Options: renormalize per target over the factors with data, or show "no verbatim evidence" as an explicit gap.
  - **Satisfaction gap:** CN/EU means and US distributions aren't comparable, and neither has sample sizes (Q-006).

### Q-005 — How are the "Source A–D" feedback channels interpreted?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context: Sources are anonymized. Observed patterns (`documents/data-inventory.md` §1) are hypotheses only:
  - **A:** multi-country (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized, possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only, third-person "Customer stated…" notes.
  - **C:** US only, structured survey prompts ("I had a minor/serious problem…", "What is…"), mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only, short, ~80% positive. Likely "what do you like" answers, **not** "what could be improved".
- This affects source-trust weighting. Don't weight sources differently until confirmed.

### Q-006 — Customer study scales
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context:
  - The CN_EU sheet has numeric means in the range ~6.5–9.9 (0–10 or 1–10?).
  - The US sheet is a 7-point distribution ("I Hate It" … "I Love It").
  - **Neither sheet has sample sizes** — ask for n per model/market.
- Needed to compare/normalize, and to judge whether differences are meaningful.

### Q-007 — Team roles & who is the "PM" in the demo?
- Owner: team

### Q-008 — Hackathon logistics
- Owner: team
- Questions: submission deadline, demo length, required format (video/live/slides), judging criteria.

### Q-010 — Does BMW accept platform/plant feasibility as part of the solution?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context:
  - The brief puts technical/engineering requirements out of scope and explicitly names "**architecture**", which arguably covers vehicle platforms.
  - D-009 (accepted) makes feasibility a blocking gate. Yet the platform mappings and plant volumes in `portfolio-reference.md` are mostly [Trade]/[Unverified].
- Options for the team (not decided):
  - (a) keep it as a blocking gate;
  - (b) non-blocking "realization context" (warn/info only);
  - (c) drop it.
- Ask the mentors which framing helps rather than hurts.

### Q-011 — How detailed can plant/platform reference data be?
- Owner: team
- Context: public sources give plant ↔ model/platform mapping and NK timing, rarely capacity or flexibility. Decide what granularity we claim, and mark the rest as assumptions.

### Q-012 — How do we demo a ~2-year continuous process in a hackathon?
- Owner: team
- Context: D-013. The feedback data has **no dates**, so real time series aren't available.
- Recommendation: simulate time with **ingest waves**, labelled clearly as a simulation:
  - **Don't split waves by source:** the channels differ systematically (Q-005), so an A/B → C/D split would show channel differences as "changes over time".
  - Instead: wave 1 = a stratified random half of the verbatims + 2024 sales; wave 2 = the other half + study + 2025 sales; wave 3 = an "event" from web research (e.g. a competitor launch or the China sales drop).
- Show the priority timeline and AI change proposals between waves.

### Q-013 — Market profile sources
- Owner: team
- Context: D-011 needs climate/usage/culture per market. Use research agents + cited sources (mobility studies, climate data, J.D. Power China/US).
- How deep do we go? EU as one market or split (DE vs. GB vs. Nordics)? Note that F70 feedback is 32% Japan and G60/G70 have KR/JP feedback (RoW).
- Recommendation: EU / US / CN (+ RoW where data exists) for the demo; the data model already supports countries.

### Q-014 — Architecture & framework choices (BLOCKING for scaffolding — discuss with team, do NOT decide alone)
- Owner: Atahan + team, in a dedicated architecture session
- Context: Atahan wants these discussed before any decision: **LangChain, LangGraph, a vector DB, a graph (knowledge graph / graph DB), and RAG**. Everything in `documents/tech-stack.md` and the storage/orchestration parts of `documents/architecture.md` is a proposal only.
- Points to prepare for the discussion (not decisions):
  - Orchestration: LangGraph (stateful graphs, human-in-the-loop interrupts, checkpoints — fits PM gates & re-prioritization loop) vs. OpenAI Agents SDK vs. plain SDK + own pipeline.
  - Retrieval: RAG over verbatims + web evidence for derivation and PM "challenge" answers; which vector store (Chroma, LanceDB, pgvector, Qdrant, sqlite-vec) and how citations stay traceable.
  - Graph: knowledge graph of source → finding → requirement → target (derivative/market/platform/plant) — graph DB (Neo4j, Kùzu) vs. relational tables + graph view.
  - Fit with constraints: $100 budget (D-010), audit trail (D-003), traceability, hackathon time.

### Q-015 — Are the BMW sales volumes real or illustrative?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context: `sales_volumes.xlsx` conflicts with public data:
  - Its values are round thousands (all but one).
  - G60/G68 China is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025, while public figures say 5 Series China (China-built, CPCA) Jan–Nov 2025 = 107,348 and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5%.
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce).
  - There is no powertrain split, although the briefing promised one.
- Until answered: use the file as BMW-internal relative weights, don't blend it with public figures, and show the conflict (`data-inventory.md` §3, `portfolio-reference.md` §4).

### Q-016 — Is driver assistance (ADAS) in scope?
- Owner: team (ask BMW mentors)
- Context:
  - BMW's process image (image_2) lists *Driver assistance* and *Powertrain* as requirement groups.
  - ADAS is a top purchase driver in China (`competitor-landscape.md` §2).
  - But "safety" is out of scope (regulatory).
- Working line (not decided): ADAS *experience* (usability, availability, comfort, trust) is in; safety/homologation performance is out.

## Resolved

### Q-009 — OpenAI models & budget → **luna for bulk, 6.1-sol for reasoning, $100 cap with guard** (D-010)
- Answered 2026-10-10: Atahan set $100 total and delegated model choice to the agent.

### Q-001 — Demo derivative/market → **portfolio-level, 5 Series deepest** (D-005)
- Answered by Atahan 2026-10-10: no single-car demo. Multi-model, multi-market architecture from the start; 5 Series (G60/G68) is the deepest example.

### Q-002 — Tech stack → **OpenAI for LLM/agents** (D-006); rest stays proposed default (D-004)
- Answered by Atahan 2026-10-10. API key provided by Atahan.

### Q-003 — Focus area → **web-enriched knowledge base + brand fit + platform/plant feasibility** (D-007, D-008, D-009)
- Answered by Atahan 2026-10-10: research competitors (offers, sales, in-demand models) and general customer expectations on the web; factor in brand image/segment and plants/platforms.

I've fixed areas 1, 2, 3 and 6 of your review list across 10 foundation files. Nothing is committed and no code was written.

**1. The brief (`challenge-brief.md`).** I added what was missing from BMW's material:
- The minimum is one derivative in one market; the remaining datasets are optional.
- BMW's three "What to demonstrate" items from the PDF.
- BMW's line that it cares about the reasoning, "not a specific workflow or technical architecture".
- A table of what BMW promised for each dataset versus what it delivered.
- A "Scope tensions" section, written plainly rather than glossed over: the platform/plant gate versus "architecture" being out of scope, driver assistance versus "safety" being out of scope, and BMW's "Business" prioritization dimension versus no business case.
- The mentor section is now marked as a paraphrase. Someone should paste the original Discord message in.

**2. The data inventory (`data-inventory.md`).** I rewrote it from the actual files:
- Counts are now real verbatims (unique IDs), not spreadsheet rows.
- Average text length is ~215–225 characters, not 300.
- Source D now reads as "what do you like" answers, not "what could be improved".
- Neither customer study has sample sizes, and the CN/EU scores are stored as numbers, not text.
- The G60 option list covers the sedan only, no Touring.
- The coverage matrix now has a Rest-of-World column. F70 feedback is about one-third Japan, and G70 has only ~19 European verbatims.
- I noted that the BMW sales file conflicts with public data (China 75k and rising there, versus 107k and falling publicly).

**3. The research docs (`portfolio-reference.md`, `competitor-landscape.md`).** I applied the 23 checked facts:
- **Corrected:** BMW's first-half 2026 group total is 1,156,742; I took it from BMW's own release PDF, which also settles a disagreement between sources.
- **Replaced:** the Lexus link (now dead) with the CarBuzz original, and the Euro NCAP citation with the European Transport Safety Council (ETSC), whose write-up actually lists those physical controls.
- **Fixed dates:** the Reuters China-EV article is from July 2026, not 2025, and I noted it compares fully-electric-only against all plug-in cars.
- **Reworded:** the production-start (SOP) dates are now worded as precisely as BMW states them.
- **Flagged as unverified or single-source:** the 7 Series range figure, the per-plant output, the model-pair sales, the Mercedes per-model figures, and the China EV production end (now marked as a rumour).

**6. Consistency.**
- `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`: questions reordered. Q-004 now lists the scoring problems found in review, including the built-in bias against China. Q-005, Q-006 and Q-010 are updated with the evidence. Q-012 now recommends random waves instead of waves split by source. I added Q-015 (are the sales numbers real?) and Q-016 (is driver assistance in scope?).
- `DECISIONS.md`: D-004's status is now "proposed", a valid value. D-009 has a note on the scope tension.
- `AGENTS.md`:
  - Rule 5 now allows the AI-score-recompute exception that D-013 already relies on.
  - Rule 9 now says whether a feasibility `fail` blocks approval is still open.
  - The quick facts are corrected.
- Requirement categories now include Powertrain and Driver Assistance (from BMW's process image), and the status rules are spelled out.
- The knowledge base gains the market-profile research agent that other files already assumed.
- `STATE.md` is updated.

I made no architecture decisions. The feasibility gate and the driver-assistance scope are written as open questions, not settled.

Still open from the review: the budget re-baseline (my estimate is about $55–150, not ~$40), the decision-hygiene wording (`tech-stack.md`'s "Choice" column, the SQLite mentions in `STATE.md` and D-010), and the usability items. One cost point, not a confidentiality one: run the `sk-proj` grep on that public checkpoint ref. If a key is in there, strangers can spend your $100.

ndustry are regularly examined, evaluated and the underlying assumptions are reviewed. The overarching corporate strategy and the strategic goals of the BMW Group serve as the reference point for the departments to define specific directions and impl

2	53 Overview of the BMW Group INNOVATIONS AND PRODUCT TECHNOLOGIES Thanks to its remarkable capacity for innovation, the BMW Group makes great strides in technological development while focusing on the needs of its customers. The Group’s innovative de
3	signs are helping to shape the future of individual mobility. In the reporting year 2025, the NEUE KLASSE made its debut with the world premiere of the BMW iX31. The all-new model generation represents a huge leap in technology, driving experience an

11	-cut-design central display, creates a clearly structured and intuitive information and control system. The further developed BMW Intelligent Personal Assistant will use Large Language Model (LLM) technology for the first time, thus allowing for natu
12	ral and context-sensitive voice interaction. The system, which is learning all the time, reacts proactively to situations on the road and helps users to configure personalised routines. This turns the vehicle into an intelligent and adaptive assistan
13	t for everyday driving. Focus on China: BMW Panoramic iDrive with Operating System X BMW Operating System X for the Chinese market offers an array of exclusive digital features, including the AI-based BMW Intelligent Personal Assistant for China. The
14	 Large Language Model (LLM) integrated into the BMW Intelligent Personal Assistant is the result of a collaboration with Chinese technology company Alibaba. As the 2025 reporting year progresses, “AI Reasoning by Deepseek” will gradually be rolled ou
15	t as an additional feature for the BMW Intelligent Personal Assistant, establishing seamless interconnectivity between the vehicle and the outside world. Digital technologies driving innovation, efficiency and the customer experience Digitalisation e
16	nables vehicle software to be kept up to date for the entire service life of the vehicle and allows further features to be added subsequently. Thanks to Remote Software Upgrade, software updates can be installed without visiting the workshop.2 This m
17	eans customers regularly receive new features in the areas of infotainment, driver assistance, comfort and safety. Furthermore, BMW ConnectedDrive upgrades enable customers to buy additional digital services after the initial vehicle purchase. These 
18	are flexible and customisable and can be activated at any time. Together with the high connectivity of current BMW models, which includes 5G technology and cloud-based services, the vehicle is becoming an integral part of its user’s digital life. 1 2

21	54 Overview of the BMW Group The new generation of vehicles gradually being rolled out in global markets, starting with the new BMW iX3*, has been systematically designed and developed as a digitally controlled product. In addition to a new on-board 
22	electrical system with a zonal architecture, AI technologies are increasingly being integrated into the vehicles for use in the infotainment systems. These innovative technologies are turning the automobile into a software-defined vehicle. Next-gener
23	ation automated driving In 2025, the Company became the first automotive manufacturer in Germany to receive international UNECE approval for innovative driver assistance systems in accordance with UN Regulation No. 171 for Driver Control Assistance S
24	ystems (DCAS). The BMW iX3* is the first model to feature the latest generation of the Highway and City Assistant. With this system, the BMW Group is upgrading the capabilities of the Highway Assistant, enabling it to operate at up to 130 km/h on sel
25	ected highways and adding extra features for driving in urban areas. At market launch in Germany, the system helps drivers to stop at red lights and to move away again automatically when they turn green. Additional functions for the complex situation
26	s often encountered in driving in urban areas are gradually being rolled out via Remote Software Upgrade. With features such as these, the BMW Group is combining continuous innovation with the highest safety standards. BMW Symbiotic Drive establishes
27	 a seamless transition between driver assistance systems and driver control, and is reaching the next stage of development in NEUE KLASSE vehicles. In addition to symbiotic steering, the BMW iX3* is the first model to feature symbiotic braking. When 
28	the driver assistance features are switched on, the driver can influence the system to suit their preferences at any time by making slight adjustments to the steering and brakes, without switching off the driver assistance features. The system remain
29	s actively supportive. The more than two dozen patent applications filed by the BMW Group as a result of the development of these technologies underscore the innovative nature of the symbiotic braking system. With advances like these, the BMW Group i
30	s living up to its claim to continually redefine the driving experience in an intelligent, safe and forwardthinking manner. Development in China for China: cooperation with Momenta New drivetrain for the NEUE KLASSE The sixth generation of BMW e-driv
31	e technology includes a new drivetrain with an all-new high-voltage battery design. It is one of the most remarkable innovations of the NEUE KLASSE. In cooperation with Momenta, a leading provider of ADAS technology in China, the BMW Group is develop
32	ing driver assistance solutions specifically for the BMW product range offered in China, starting with the NEUE KLASSE. In addition to advanced, highly efficient electric motors, it incorporates completely new high-voltage batteries with cylindrical 
33	cells. The batteries increase range by 30% compared with the fifth generation, with an even greater improvement in some models. In the case of the new BMW iX3*, this means a range of up to 805 km (based on the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test
34	 Procedure, WLTP). The charging speed is 30% faster and the cylindrical cells offer a 20% increase in volumetric energy density compared with the prismatic cells used in the fifth generation. This collaboration is based on the BMW philosophy of “smar
35	t, symbiotic and safe”, combining intelligent interaction, control and driver assistance systems to ensure maximum benefit and safety for the driver in every situation. The BMW Group and Momenta are working together on developing a Level 2+ driver as
36	sistance system that covers all scenarios – from leaving a car park to navigating around urban areas and from the highway back to the car park. The partnership focuses on software development and integration specifically tailored to Chinese road netw
37	orks, traffic conditions and user expectations, and involves making use of advanced AI algorithms and data-driven development methods. * ↗ Consumption and Carbon Disclosures.

39	55 Overview of the BMW Group The role of charging as a key enabler for electromobility In addition to the evolution in charging capacity in the NEUE KLASSE, the BMW Group is focusing on all other aspects relating to the customer charging experience. 
40	A well-developed, customer-friendly charging infrastructure will pave the way for the rapid and widespread use of electromobility. It is for this reason that the BMW Group remains committed to achieving standardised framework conditions and is develo
41	ping and supporting offers that enable comprehensive and customer-friendly charging. Customers will be offered solutions for charging at home. The BMW Group also supports the expansion of public charging infrastructure through its cooperations. The B
42	MW Group has put its own large charging network in place for its employees at its locations in Germany. Integrating electrified vehicles in the energy system The BMW Group conducts its own research and development with the aim of integrating electrif
43	ied vehicles into the power grid. This research focuses on smart charging technologies such as those optimised for load, solar power or price, as well as bidirectional charging. ↗ BMW ChargeForward enables customers in the USA to synchronise their ch
44	arging behaviour with the current grid load and the use of renewable energy. The technology has been available to all drivers of electrified vehicles in the USA since late 2023. In this context, the joint venture ChargeScape LLC was founded in the US
45	A together with our partners Ford, Honda and Nissan in 2024. ChargeScape provides an open software platform for OEMs and energy providers that offers US customers smart home charging of their electric vehicles. This is intended to optimise the use of
46	 renewable energies and help to stabilise the grid. Thanks to the ChargeForward service and the integration with ChargeScape, BMW customers in the USA have access to smart charging programmes from a current roster of seven energy suppliers. This also
47	 opens up access to smart charging rewards, which offers users incentives for smart, grid-friendly charging. Customers in Europe have the option of working with a range of energy suppliers to optimise their charging activities. With its Remote Chargi
48	ng Control service, the BMW Group enables affiliated electricity suppliers to offer smart charging features such as price-optimised charging. Access to public charging networks With BMW and MINI Charging, the BMW Group offers its customers attractive
49	 EV charging tariffs and convenient charging solutions whether they are on the road, at home or at work. Customers can use a large number of public charging points via their BMW or MINI charging card and the My BMW or MINI app. Digital Charging Solut
50	ions GmbH (DCS) provides broad access to various charging networks throughout Europe. DCS is one of Europe’s leading providers of digital charging solutions and a joint venture between the BMW Group, Mercedes-Benz and bp. BMW and MINI customers have 
51	access to 3.4 million charging points1 worldwide through the navigation system or the relevant vehicle app. In Europe alone, easy access to a network with over 1 million charging points is provided through the public BMW/MINI Charging service. In Eur
52	ope, these also include fast-charging stations run by IONITY, a company set up by the BMW Group, with a charging capacity of between 350 and 400 kilowatts (kW). IONITY currently operates 840 stations with more than 5,900 charging points in a total of
53	 24 countries, which are publicly accessible, brand-independent and designed in accordance with the European Combined Charging System (CCS) charging standard. They are also powered by 100% electricity from renewable sources2. In addition to the BMW G
54	roup, Mercedes-Benz, Ford, Porsche, Volkswagen, Audi, Hyundai, Kia and BlackRock are all involved in the long-established IONITY joint venture. IONITY offers an efficient, high-power charging network for electric vehicles right across Europe. joined 
55	IONNA as an additional partner in July 2024. The first charging stations went into operation in late 2024. At the end of the reporting year, 80 charging stations accommodating more than 760 charging points were operational in the USA. In addition, an
56	 adapter allowing all-electric vehicles from BMW Group brands to be charged with charging infrastructure using the NACS connectors that are widespread in the USA was introduced in 2025. In March 2024, BMW Brilliance Automotive Ltd. (BBA) and Mercedes
57	-Benz China founded Beijing IONCHI New Energy Technology Ltd. with a view to developing the charging infrastructure in the Chinese market. By the end of 2025, the network had already grown to more than 460 charging stations with over 2,500 charging p
58	oints. The goal is further expansion, with a particular focus on high-performance charging. Additional charging stations are being set up, with particular attention being paid to regions with high concentrations of electrified vehicles. The networks 
59	are available to drivers of all brands but offer extras such as additional charging speed and a booking service to customers driving vehicles from the partner brands involved. The BMW Group also promotes the use of renewable energy. For each charging
60	 process conducted via BMW and MINI Charging in Europe, the equivalent amount of energy consumed is fed into the power grid as electricity from renewable sources2, which is certified via Energy Attribute Certificates (EACs). The BMW Group has also ex
61	panded its cooperation arrangements aimed at extending charging infrastructure in the USA and China in recent years. In late 2023, the BMW Group set up IONNA together with General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz and Stellantis. The partner
62	s are working together with the aim of establishing a public charging network in the USA and Canada. Toyota 1 2 Total number of charging points displayed on BMW front ends (vehicle and app). The network can be accessed by registered customers whereve
63	r a local partner is available. See ↗ Glossary for definition of electricity from renewable sources.

65	56 Overview of the BMW Group Bidirectional charging: making the BMW iX3* a flexible energy storage device at home and a mobile power bank on the road In addition to faster public charging, the bidirectional charging functionality is another major inn
66	ovation in the BMW iX3*. The energy stored in the high-voltage battery can be used not only for the drivetrain but also outside the vehicle. — Vehicle-to-Home (V2H): With the new bidirectional BMW Wallbox Professional, the BMW iX3* can, when combined
67	 with a domestic photovoltaic (PV) installation, be used as a system to store homegenerated solar power. Thanks to the smart connection between the Wallbox and the house, electricity can flow in both directions, either to charge the vehicle’s high-vo
68	ltage battery or to supply domestic electrical appliances. This gives customers a way to cut both their charging costs and their domestic electricity bills. — Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G): The BMW Group and E.ON are continuing their long-standing strategic 
69	partnership. As of February 2026, private customers will be able to order the complete product package, comprising the BMW Wallbox Professional, E.ON’s V2G electricity tariff and the necessary smart meter system. This offer will allow BMW NEUE KLASSE
70	 electric vehicles to be integrated into the public electricity grid, starting with the BMW iX3*. Customers will see financial benefits for every hour that their vehicles are plugged in, and they will be contributing to the future of energy at the sa

72	ultaneously. Combining the newly developed Multifunction Charger (MFC) with the Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) discharge adapter opens up a variety of options for flexible use. From pilot fleet to series production: the new BMW iX5 Hydrogen The BMW Group is l
73	aunching a vehicle with five different drivetrain technologies for the first time. The new BMW X5, which the Company will be presenting in 2026, will enable customers to choose between a battery-powered drivetrain, plug-in hybrid, petrol, diesel and,
74	 from 2028 onwards, hydrogen fuel cell technology. Following successful international trials with the pilot fleet, the plan is for the BMW iX5 Hydrogen to launch in 2028, making it the first hydrogen-powered series production model. The drivetrain te
75	chnology is based on the third generation of the fuel cell system developed by the BMW Group in collaboration with the Toyota Motor Corporation. This technological development allows for a more compact design and a more powerful and efficient system,
76	 and it increases range and power output while also cutting energy consumption. The first prototypes are already being built at the BMW Group’s Competence Centres in Munich and at its Steyr plant. The BMW Group plant in Landshut is also supplying add
77	itional components for the drivetrain system. In November 2025, the BMW Group received a grant for research and development on its fuel cell technology from the German Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV) and the Bavarian State Ministry of Economic Af
78	fairs, Regional Development and Energy (StMWi) as part of the European IPCEI (Important Projects of Common European Interest) initiative. This funding will help to cover the considerable development costs. Next steps in the development of all-solid-s
79	tate batteries Since 2022, the BMW Group and Solid Power, Inc. have been jointly investing in the development of all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) as part of their technology transfer agreement. The latest milestone was the integration of large pure 
80	ASSB cells manufactured by Solid Power in a BMW i7 test vehicle. Samsung SDI joined the project in October 2025 and will be carrying out development and validation of the ASSB technology in the automotive sector. The new collaboration marks a crucial
81	 step towards ASSB technology and pools the complementary technical strengths of three industry leaders. As part of the agreement, Solid Power will supply sulphide-based solid electrolytes to Samsung SDI. Samsung SDI will integrate these as separator
82	s and catholytes and use them for cell production. These cells will then be assessed using performance parameters to determine whether they meet the requirements agreed between Samsung SDI and the BMW Group. Finally, the partners will work towards de
83	veloping and manufacturing ASSB cells that can be integrated into a future generation of evaluation vehicles. HVO100: a solution for fleet customers In addition to the electrification of the vehicle fleet, fuels based on renewable raw materials, know
84	n as carbon-neutral fuels (CNFs), offer potential for CO2e reduction. It is also possible to improve the carbon footprints of existing vehicles in Europe by increasing the renewable content of the fuel they use. The BMW Group is trialling a new techn
85	ical solution with the goal of verifying that the diesel BMW models in a fleet can be run exclusively on HVO100. HVO stands for “hydrotreated vegetable oil”, while the suffix “100” indicates that it is used as a 100% undiluted fuel. Data on the refue
86	lling process from the vehicle are compared against data from the fleet operator’s payment system. The aim is to provide a complete record of the fuel used to fill up the vehicle. This represents a major step towards a CNF-only fleet for fleet custom
87	ers. The first contracts with operators of large diesel BMW fleets in Germany and Italy are due to be signed soon. These test fleets, alongside the internal fleet already launched by the BMW Group, will deliver important data and findings that will h
88	elp to refine the technology further. * ↗ Consumption and Carbon Disclosures. 
89	######## PAGE 57
90	57 Overview of the BMW Group All diesel models produced in Germany since the first quarter of 2025 have been fuelled with HVO100 before being delivered to sales partners. This underscores the BMW Group’s commitment to making practical decarbonisation
91	 a reality today. In addition, Neste MY Renewable Diesel™ HVO100 is being used at BMW Group plants in Munich, Dingolfing, Regensburg and Leipzig. According to Finnish company Neste, which makes the fuel, it is capable of cutting well-to-wheel CO2e em
92	issions by as much as 90% compared with fossil-based diesel. Lower CO2e fuels for petrol vehicles as well The BMW Group, Lother GmbH and German eFuel One GmbH are working in partnership with the aim of promoting the use of petrol with lower CO2e emis
93	sions. The partners are confident that advanced biofuels and RFNBOs (renewable fuels of non-biological origin) such as e-fuels can be part of a more climate-friendly future for mobility. This highlights the BMW Group’s comprehensive approach of belie
94	ving that all technologies, from electromobility to diesel and petrol engines using renewable fuels, can play a part in climate change mitigation. The BMW Group is planning to use e-fuels as first-fill fuels for new vehicles with petrol engines at se
95	lected production sites in Germany as of 2028. All BMW Group vehicles with petrol engines and approval for E10 can run on this type of fuel. German eFuel One GmbH is planning to build Germany’s first commercial production facility for e-fuels. In thi
96	s case, imported e-methanol is to be used to produce high-quality MtG (methanolto-gasoline), a renewable alternative to fossil fuels. This type of e-fuel is a synthetic petrol based on the DIN EN 228 standard for E10 petrol, made entirely from non-fo
97	ssil-based CO2. It offers an alternative to conventional fossil-based petrol and is compatible with existing vehicles – with no need for any technical modifications. The trend research conducted by the Technology Offices enables the BMW Group to anti
98	cipate the technological developments of tomorrow. The results are made publicly available in the ↗ Trend Radar, where scientific institutions, start-ups and potential partners can make use of them. Global tech expertise at the international network 
99	of BMW Group Technology Offices From Silicon Valley to Shanghai, from Seoul to Tel Aviv – the BMW Group’s Tech Offices are key hubs in the Company’s international innovation network. Their mission is to identify groundbreaking technologies in their r
100	egions and apply them to create sustainable solutions for transport, digitalisation and the environment. The BMW Group Tech Office in Silicon Valley is located in one of the world’s foremost centres of innovation. Working closely with top tech compan
101	ies, start-ups, venture capitalists and universities gives the Company early access to the latest trends, groundbreaking technologies and digital business models. The teams at the Tech Offices work across multiple disciplines and focus on technology 
102	scouting, open innovation and research, as well as the development of proof-of-concept projects. Together with start-ups, universities, industry partners and tech giants, they help to create pioneering innovations that can be fed directly into the BM
103	W Group’s global research and development operations. Each Tech Office focuses on a specific field – from artificial intelligence and software-defined vehicles to electromobility and smart city ecosystems. Maintaining a presence in the world’s leadin
104	g centres of innovation ensures that the BMW Group remains agile, forward-looking and innovative. With their global perspective and specialist expertise within their respective regions, the Tech Offices are making a crucial contribution to technologi
105	cal excellence and the Company’s pursuit of innovation leadership. Global dialogue with start-ups is an important source of inspiration for the BMW Group. ↗ BMW i Ventures invests in technology start-ups. The ↗ BMW Startup Garage serves as the BMW Gr
106	oup’s venture client unit and is tasked with finding innovations that represent a significant benefit for products, services, systems and processes. The purpose of the programme is to evaluate start-ups and to enable them to become suppliers and part
107	ners. The team is mostly concerned with artificial intelligence, software development and what the user experience will look like in the future. At the same time, it maintains partnerships and conducts pilot projects to evaluate new technologies in c
108	lose collaboration with the BMW Group’s research and development operations. By precisely analysing trends and thereby identifying opportunities at an early stage, the Silicon Valley Tech Office creates strategic added value for the BMW Group. With a
109	n open-minded approach, vision and creativity, it is shaping the technologies and experiences that will define the products, services and customer journey of the future at the BMW Group. Software expertise at the BMW Group The BMW Group began develop
110	ing its own software more than 20 years ago, and it has been systematically expanding its global network ever since. A diverse engineer ecosystem is now operating at the Group’s international technology sites and was recently joined by the new BMW Te
111	chWorks IT and software hubs in Romania and India. ↗ Locations The teams are working on global IT projects covering the entire value chain and are also developing the software-defined vehicle (SDV) – the next generation of connected vehicles. 
112	######## PAGE 58
113	58 Overview of the BMW Group Artificial intelligence AI is a key technology that can make a substantial contribution to efforts to improve efficiency, quality and customer satisfaction and will play a major role in advancing the digital transformatio
114	n of the BMW Group. A self-service platform enables employees to develop AI-based solutions rapidly. AI agents and agentic workflows that can handle complex tasks largely by themselves are being used with increasing regularity. AI is becoming a major
115	 feature in vehicles, with smart voice assistants, personalised recommendations and driver assistance features delivering a steady stream of improvements to interactions between customer and vehicle. AI applications along the value chain include the 
116	following examples: — Development: image-generating AI for design processes — Coding support for IT and vehicle development — Communication with customers: in-vehicle voice applications, AI-assisted customer chat (BMW/MINI Assistant) — Marketing, Sal
117	es and Financial Services: AI-generated marketing copy and images, AI-assisted sales and customer support processes — Service and support: AI knowledge management — Purchasing: AI-assisted bid comparison, knowledge management, support for internal pu
118	rchasing processes — Production: AI quality platform to analyse sensor and image data in real time, pilot project involving humanoid robots automated driving. The joint development will celebrate its market launch in 2026 with the BMW iX3* and will s
119	ubsequently be rolled out across the entire BMW model range. Within the terms of the cooperation, some 1,300 specialists are working together at various locations worldwide, including sites in Germany, the USA, Sweden, China, Romania and the BMW Test
120	 Centre in Sokolov in the Czech Republic. Continuing their long-term supplier relationship, the BMW Group has collaborated with Valeo Comfort and Driving Assistance SAS since early 2023 on the joint development of highly automated parking functions. 
121	Since the launch of the first BMW voice assistant (BMW Intelligent Personal Assistant) in 2018, voice interaction has become an increasingly important part of the BMW iDrive display and operating concept. The next generation of the voice assistant is
122	 based on Alexa Custom Assistant technology. This new technology has been included in vehicles ex-factory since 2024 and is available for previously manufactured automobiles via Remote Software Upgrade, facilitating a more natural dialogue between dr
123	ivers and vehicles. The HERE mapping service was acquired by BMW, Audi and Mercedes-Benz in 2015. Bosch, Aumovio, Intel, Mitsubishi (MC), NTT (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation of Japan) and Pioneer are also current shareholders. The partici
124	pation in HERE ensures access to scalable, high-resolution maps for existing and new vehicles as well as geodata services and navigation software. Worldwide cooperations and partnerships To ensure its long-term success, the BMW Group enters into targ
125	eted cooperations and partnerships with companies from various industries. Several of the Group’s largest collaborations and investments are listed below. Since 2022, the BMW Group and Qualcomm Technologies have been working together to develop solut

n hybrid drivetrains as well as conventional combustion engines on a single line; this enables the Company to tailor the product range to suit a wide variety of customer wishes and needs. The production system is based on the strategic vision of the 
BMW iFACTORY, with a keen focus on electrification, profitability, sustainability and digitalisation. People will continue to form the basis in the future of production. The BMW iFACTORY utilises innovative technologies that facilitate flexible, effi
