# BMW Group Report 2025 — extract for the knowledge base

**Source:** BMW Group Report 2025 (published Mar 2026, PDF created 2 Mar 2026, 434 pages), https://www.bmwgroup.com/content/dam/grpw/websites/bmwgroup_com/ir/downloads/en/2026/bericht/BMW-Group-Report-2025-en.pdf. Retrieved 2026-10-10.
**Trust tier:** T1 (official OEM annual report, audited parts by PwC). **Page numbers** = printed page = PDF page.
**Why:** BMW support (2026-10-10) recommended the report for (1) market & sales data and (2) product strategy & R&D. Only these two areas are extracted; the financial statements are skipped.

**How to use:**
- **Evidence:** these are evidence for *market context and BMW's strategic direction*.
- **Not feasibility:** they are **not** engineering feasibility proof, and they don't turn engineering topics into customer requirements (scope: `challenge-brief.md` → Scope tensions, Q-010).
- **Rounding:** figures are as printed; the report rounds per commercial practice (p. 7).
- **Supersedes:** this final report supersedes the provisional January 2026 press-release figures (`portfolio-reference.md` §3).

---

## 1. Market & sales data

### 1.1 Deliveries 2025 (final)

| Metric | 2024 | 2025 | Δ | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BMW Group (Automotive) deliveries | 2,450,854 | **2,463,681** | +0.5% | 9, 12, 77 |
| BMW brand | 2,200,217 | 2,169,739 | −1.4% | 12, 77 |
| MINI | 244,925 | 288,278 | +17.7% | 12, 80 |
| Rolls-Royce | 5,712 | 5,664 | −0.8% | 12, 80 |
| BMW M GmbH | 206,587 | 213,449 | +3.3% | 79 |

- **Final vs. provisional:** the January press release had 2,463,715 / 2,169,761 (provisional). The report's figures are final, so the "typo" assumption in `portfolio-reference.md` §5 was wrong.
- **BMW brand without China:** sales grew **+4.2%** (p. 78).
- **BMW brand in China:** monthly deliveries were "roughly 50,000 units" at year-end (p. 78).

### 1.2 Regional trends (BMW Group incl. Rolls-Royce, in 1,000 units, p. 78)

| Region | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | **2025** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Europe | 949.1 | 878.5 | 943.0 | 948.5 | **1,017.6** |
| – Germany | 266.8 | 254.3 | 272.6 | 265.7 | 288.5 |
| – UK | 164.3 | 157.3 | 159.2 | 168.8 | 171.4 |
| Americas | 451.7 | 441.5 | 482.0 | 482.7 | **509.9** |
| – USA | 368.0 | 363.5 | 397.3 | 399.3 | **419.2** |
| Asia | 1,067.9 | 1,031.0 | 1,073.1 | 963.6 | **874.1** |
| – China | 847.9 | 793.5 | 826.3 | 715.2 | **626.0** |
| Other markets | 52.8 | 48.6 | 56.1 | 56.1 | 62.1 |
| Total | 2,521.5 | 2,399.6 | 2,554.2 | 2,450.9 | 2,463.7 |

- **Growth by region:** Europe +7.3%, Americas +5.6%, China −12.5% (p. 77). China has declined three years in a row since 2023.
- **BMW brand, share of sales by market** (2025, with 2024 in brackets; p. 78):

  | Market | 2025 (2024) |
  |---|---|
  | China | **25.4% (29.2%)** |
  | USA | 17.0% (16.3%) |
  | Germany | 11.7% (10.8%) |
  | UK | 7.0% (6.9%) |
  | Italy | 3.6% |
  | France | 3.5% |
  | South Korea | 3.5% |
  | Other | 28.3% |

- **Total market growth 2025** (all vehicle groups served by BMW; p. 67):

  | Market | Change |
  |---|---|
  | Europe | +2.2% (DE +1.4, FR −5.1, IT −2.5, ES +13.1, UK +3.5) |
  | USA | +2.4% |
  | China | +3.2% |
  | Japan | +3.3% |
  | South Korea | +4.8% |
  | World | +3.3% (82.3 M) |

  - **China market vs. BMW:** the market grew while BMW fell 12.5%.
  - **China's growth segment:** growth was "dominated by vehicles priced at 150,000 renminbi or less" and the "trend toward local manufacturers continued" (p. 67).

### 1.3 Deliveries by model series (BMW brand, p. 79)

| Model series | 2024 | 2025 | Δ | Share 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1/2 Series | 198,226 | 214,175 | +8.0% | 9.9% |
| 3/4 Series | 519,228 | 477,180 | −8.1% | 22.0% |
| **5/6 Series** | 250,674 | **299,582** | **+19.5%** | 13.8% |
| **7/8 Series** | 56,542 | **53,399** | **−5.6%** | 2.5% |
| Z4 | 10,482 | 9,744 | −7.0% | 0.4% |
| X1/X2 | 413,386 | 436,769 | +5.7% | 20.1% |
| X3/X4 | 370,198 | 321,186 | −13.2% | 14.8% |
| X5/X6 | 275,318 | 256,941 | −6.7% | 11.8% |
| X7 | 59,949 | 58,089 | −3.1% | 2.7% |
| iX | 38,365 | 35,055 | −8.6% | 1.6% |
| XM | 7,813 | 7,608 | −2.6% | 0.4% |
| **BMW total** | 2,200,217 | 2,169,739 | −1.4% | 100% |

- **X family vs. sedans** (sums of the rows above):

  | | 2025 | Share | Change vs 2024 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | X models (X1/X2, X3/X4, X5/X6, X7, iX, XM) | 1,115,648 | ~51% | −3.9% |
  | Sedans/coupés (1/2, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, Z4) | 1,054,080 | ~49% | +1.3% |

  - **Caveat:** these sums are our calculation, not BMW's, and the pairs mix body styles (e.g. 2 Series Active Tourer, 4 Series Gran Coupé).
- **Model highlights:**
  - The 5 Series (with the X2) achieved "strong growth rates" (p. 78).
  - The 7/8 pair is the only premium sedan line declining (−5.6%).
  - Almost one in ten BMWs delivered was an M model (p. 79).

### 1.4 Electrification / EV adoption

| Metric | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Group BEV share of deliveries | 4.1% | 9.0% | 14.7% | 17.4% | **17.9%** | 9 |
| Group electrified (BEV+PHEV) share | 13.0% | 18.1% | 22.2% | 24.2% | **26.1%** | 12 |
| Group BEV units | 103,854 | 215,752 | 375,716 | 426,536 | 442,059 (+3.6%) | 12 |

- **Group PHEV:** 200,012 (+20.0%), share 8.1%. Electrified total 642,071 (+8.2%) (p. 77).
- **BMW brand:** BEV 335,528 (**−8.9%**, 15.5% of the brand); PHEV 199,883 (**+21.8%**, 9.2%) (p. 79). BEV growth came from MINI (105,529 BEV, +87.9%, 36.6% of MINI; p. 80). **PHEV is BMW's growing electrified powertrain.**
- **Model-level adoption:**
  - iX1 was the BMW brand's most successful BEV; >25% of X1 deliveries were BEV.
  - Almost half of 4 Series (Gran Coupé) deliveries were the i4.
  - iX3 (NK) preorders "extend well into 2026" (p. 78).
- **Production:** electrified 597,309 (−8.2%), of which BEV 391,693 (−18.7%) (p. 61).
- **Targets and outlook:**
  - Strategic target: **>50% BEV share of deliveries by 2030**, "albeit with regional differences" (p. 3, 46).
  - 2026 outlook: BEV share "in line with last year's level" (p. 263).
  - Markets are "highly fragmented … demand, especially for electric vehicles, also depends on regional factors": charging infrastructure, cost benefits, energy prices (p. 44).

### 1.5 2026 outlook (as of Mar 2026, p. 263–264)
- **Deliveries:** Group deliveries on a par with 2025. Growth potential in Europe and the USA.
- **China:**
  - BMW "can reach the prior year's level" by stabilising transaction prices.
  - But the market is expected *below* 2025: EV subsidy cuts (especially ≤ CNY 150k) and price regulation (SAMR, Feb 2026).
  - Reality check: actual H1 2026 China was −20.4% (`portfolio-reference.md` §3.5), so the outlook was optimistic.
- **USA:** BEV sales expected to go **down** due to regulatory changes.
- **Europe:** expected to provide most of the market growth (CO₂ rules, subsidies for electrified vehicles).
- **Spending:** R&D expenditure, capex and costs "will be reduced further" in 2026 (p. 264).

### 1.6 Target persona & market prioritization — what the report does and doesn't give
- **It does:**
  - Market weights (§1.2 share of sales).
  - Powertrain trend per brand (§1.4).
  - Model-series momentum (§1.3).
  - BMW's view of customer trends (p. 42):
    - customers shape vehicle requirements around "the digital ecosystems they use daily";
    - "software updates and upgrades have become standard";
    - automated driving is "one of the key expectation[s]", with regional differences in speed;
    - vehicle ownership depends on income, household size and location.
- **It doesn't:** **no demographic/persona data, no per-model regional split, no customer-satisfaction scores** (p. 188–189 describe the survey *processes* only).

---

## 2. Product strategy & R&D

### 2.1 R&D investment priorities

| Metric | 2024 | 2025 | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| R&D expenditure | €9,078 m | **€8,319 m** (−8.4%) | 70, 71, 81 |
| R&D expenditure ratio (% of revenues) | 6.4% | 6.2% | 10, 71 |
| Capitalisation rate | 38.8% | 41.2% | 71 |

- **Focus:** R&D is "related primarily to the **cross-series digitalisation and electrification** of the vehicle fleet". It includes development of **NEUE KLASSE models such as the BMW iX3 and the successors to the BMW X5 and the BMW 7 Series** (p. 70, 81).
- **2026:** R&D expenditure "will be reduced further" (p. 264).
- **Strategic focus areas:**
  1. Technology-open drivetrains with a strong electromobility focus.
  2. Digitalisation of customer interfaces and related products/services.
  3. Sustainability / circular economy (p. 44).
- **Quality programme** "Q3 – Passion for Perfection": quality and reliability are named key factors for customer satisfaction (p. 45).
- **Partners:**
  - Momenta (China ADAS).
  - Qualcomm (automated driving, launching 2026 with the iX3, "subsequently … rolled out across the entire BMW model range"; ~1,300 specialists).
  - Valeo (automated parking) (p. 47, 54, 58).

### 2.2 NEUE KLASSE platform strategy
- **Roll-out:**
  - The NK "technology toolkit and the new design language will be rolled out across the **entire vehicle portfolio, encompassing all drivetrain types, by the end of the decade**" (p. 46).
  - "By 2027, **40 new and revised models** featuring NEUE KLASSE technologies and the new design language" (p. 53).
- **Architecture:**
  - The first NK model (iX3, built in Debrecen) is based on the **"new cluster architecture (NCAR)", focused entirely on BEVs** (p. 46). This is BMW's own platform name; trade press uses others (`portfolio-reference.md` §1).
  - The aim is to "gradually transfer the new vehicle architecture to the global production network over the next years" (p. 59).
- **Model timing:** second NK model i3: Munich, 2026 (p. 53, 59). Munich goes 100% electric by 2027 (p. 47). Spartanburg: ≥6 all-electric X models by 2030 (p. 59).
- **Gen6 eDrive vs. the fifth generation:**
  - Range +30% (iX3 up to **805 km WLTP**).
  - Charging speed +30%.
  - Cylindrical cells with +20% volumetric energy density (p. 54).
  - Gen6 battery assembly: Debrecen (2025), then Irlbach-Straßkirchen, Woodruff/Spartanburg, San Luis Potosí, Shenyang (p. 47, 59).
- **Customer-facing NK technologies:**
  - **BMW Panoramic iDrive:** Panoramic Vision across the full windscreen width, optional 3D head-up display, 17.9″ central display (p. 53).
  - **BMW Operating System X:** in-house, AOSP-based; "high degree of personalisation, regular over-the-air updates and seamless integration of the My BMW app" (p. 53).
  - **BMW Intelligent Personal Assistant with LLM technology:** proactive, personalised routines (p. 53). Alexa Custom Assistant-based since 2024, retrofittable via Remote Software Upgrade (p. 58); Alexa+ (p. 29).
  - **Heart of Joy:** driving-dynamics control unit; "enhances the driving experience" plus efficiency/range (p. 46).
  - **Zonal E/E architecture, "software-defined vehicle"** (p. 54).
  - **Highway & City Assistant:** up to 130 km/h on selected highways; stops at red lights and pulls away in Germany. First UN R171 (DCAS) approval in Germany. **Symbiotic Drive:** steering + braking input without switching the assistant off (p. 54).
  - **Bidirectional charging** on the iX3: V2H, V2G (E.ON offer from Feb 2026), V2L (p. 56).
- **NK in China** ("in China, for China and with China"; p. 28–29, 53–54):
  - iX3 Long Wheelbase: premiere Auto China, April 2026; market entry H2 2026.
  - OS X China has ~70% locally developed software.
  - Amap navigation.
  - LLMs from Alibaba and DeepSeek.
  - Huawei Digital Key, HiCar, and the **My BMW App based on HarmonyOS NEXT**.
  - Momenta L2+ "all scenarios" ADAS tailored to Chinese roads and "user expectations".
  - Media feedback on the iX3 China version: "digital features proving particularly popular" (p. 28).
- **Other drivetrains:**
  - The X5 (presented 2026) will offer five drivetrains: BEV, PHEV, petrol, diesel, hydrogen from 2028. iX5 Hydrogen in 2028 (p. 28, 46, 56).
  - Combustion engines continue alongside BEVs (p. 42, 46).
  - 16 BEV models on offer by end of 2025. iX up to 701 km WLTP; i4 facelift up to 613 km WLTP (p. 46).

### 2.3 ConnectedDrive & My BMW App
- **What the report says (qualitative only):**
  - **Remote Software Upgrade** delivers new features in "infotainment, driver assistance, comfort and safety". Availability depends on "country, model, equipment and software version" (p. 53).
  - **ConnectedDrive upgrades** let customers "buy additional digital services after the initial vehicle purchase" (p. 53). For brand-fit rules on paywalled hardware, see `competitor-landscape.md` §4.
  - 5G and cloud-based services (p. 53).
  - The My BMW app shows driving-style efficiency and is a charging/payment and support channel (p. 44, 55, 189).
- **Charging network access** via the app/navigation (p. 55):
  - 3.4 M charging points worldwide; >1 M in Europe.
  - IONITY: 840 stations / >5,900 points.
  - IONNA (US): 80 stations / >760 points; NACS adapter in 2025.
  - IONCHI (China): >460 stations / >2,500 points.
- **No usage metrics:** **the report contains no ConnectedDrive or My BMW App usage metrics** (users, downloads, upgrade take-rates, OTA reach). Don't cite any such numbers to this source. If needed, research them separately (T1/T2, with a citation).

---

## 3. Production network (bonus — verifies `portfolio-reference.md`)
- **Plant output** (2025, incl. pre-series; **[BMW] p. 61**), confirming the bmwblog figures:

  | Plant | 2025 output | Change |
  |---|---|---|
  | Spartanburg | 412,799 | +4.2% |
  | Regensburg | 356,901 | |
  | Tiexi | 330,691 | |
  | Dingolfing | **279,553** | −6.1% |

  | Oxford | 124,283 | |

  | Partner plants | 12,216 | |
  | **Total** | 2,456,561 | −2.3% |

- **2025 production programme per plant** (p. 60):
  - Dingolfing: 4 Series, 5 Series, i5, 7 Series, i7, **8 Series**, M, iX. This settles the 8 Series conflict for 2025.
  - Leipzig: 1 Series, 2 Series, MINI Countryman.
  - Dadong: 5 Series, i5, iX3, X5.
  - Tiexi: 2 Series, 3 Series, i3, X1, iX1, X3.

- **Inconsistency inside the report:** the p. 60 table lists Debrecen as "BMW iX1", while the text on p. 46 and p. 59 says Debrecen builds the NK **iX3**. Treat p. 60 as an error.
- **Network size:** 32 plants in 15 countries; BMW Brilliance plants mainly build for the local Chinese market (p. 60).

## 4. Conflicts with other knowledge-base docs
1. **Group/brand 2025 totals:** final 2,463,681 / 2,169,739 vs. provisional 2,463,715 / 2,169,761 (press release). → Use the final figures.
2. **X5 / 7 Series successors:**

   - Trade press says the next X5 (G65) stays on an upgraded CLAR (`portfolio-reference.md` §1.2).
   - Possible reading: NK *technology/design* on a CLAR-derived architecture.
   - Unresolved; relevant to the G70 successor.
3. **China outlook vs. actuals:** the report expected China deliveries at the prior-year level; H1 2026 was −20.4%.
4. **BMW sales file:** `sales_volumes.xlsx` has G60/G68 CN 2025 rising, while BMW reports the 5/6 Series up globally but China overall −12.5% (Q-015).

s=s.rstrip('\n')+'''

## D-014 — Budget plan re-baselined (supersedes D-010 estimate & thresholds)
- Date: 2026-10-10
- Decided by: agent (delegated by Atahan: model/budget planning; Atahan asked for the fix)
- Status: accepted
- Context: Review found D-010's ≈$40 too low. It ignored reasoning tokens (billed as output), per-target fan-out (requirements × targets × checks), and that reasoning models issue several billed search calls per request. Its thresholds were also inconsistent: a $90 hard stop left only $15 of the "$25 demo reserve".
- Prices: re-checked 2026-10-10 on developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, per 1M tokens (input / cached / output):

| Model | Standard | Flex = Batch (-50%) |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6-luna` | $0.10 / $0.01 / $0.50 | $0.05 / $0.005 / $0.25 |
| `gpt-6.1-sol` | $2.00 / $0.10 / $10.00 | $1.00 / $0.05 / $5.00 |
| `text-embedding-3-small` | $0.02 | $0.01 (Batch) |

  - Web search: $10 / 1k billed calls + content tokens at model input rates.
  - Cache writes cost 1.25× input (luna/sol). The minimum cacheable prefix is 1,024 tokens; the cache lives 30 min.

- Decision: the model choice from D-010 stays. The plan changes as follows:
  - **Flex** for same-day offline jobs; **Batch** only for overnight jobs (24 h window). Interactive and web-research calls run on Standard (Batch support for `web_search` is undocumented).
  - **Scoring is deterministic** (no LLM). LLMs only write rationale.
  - **Fit checks:** luna does the first pass on every target. sol runs only on `fail`, **once per requirement** (all its targets in one call), not per target.
  - **Web search capped in billed calls (1,000 total)**, not requests. Cap tool calls per request, and count calls from the response.
  - **Reasoning effort:** luna `none`/`low` for classification and extraction. sol `low` by default, `medium` only for derivation/projection; `high`+ needs a team OK.
  - **`max_output_tokens` on every call.**
  - **Pilot before full runs:** 50 verbatims + 5 requirements. Measure real tokens, then re-estimate this table in `STATE.md`.

- Estimate, with explicit assumptions (3 dev runs unless stated):

| Workstream | Assumptions | Tier | Est. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Classify/extract 10,128 verbatims | 25 per call (406 calls); 3.4k in (2k prompt + 25×55); 4k out (160/verbatim incl. reasoning); ×3 | luna Flex | $1.4 |
| Embeddings | 1.5 M tokens ×3 | embed | $0.1 |
| Cluster labels | 300 × (2.1k in / 0.5k out) luna + top-50 × (3k / 1.5k) sol; ×3 | Flex | $1.8 |
| Web research | 1,000 billed calls ($10) + 20k content tokens/call (luna) + 1.5k out/call | luna Std | $13 |
| Requirement derivation + future-need projection | 100 reqs × (15k in / 6k out incl. reasoning) × 3 | sol Flex | $13.5 |
| Fit checks | 1,600 luna checks (4k / 1.5k) per run + sol on ~20 failing reqs (8k / 4k); ×3 | Flex | $4.4 |
| Prioritization rationale | per run: luna 400 targets (3k / 0.8k) + sol top-20 changes (5k / 3k); 6 runs (3 dev + 3 demo waves) | Std | $6.5 |
| PM challenge / edit (dev + demo) | 150 calls × (20k in, ~50% cached / 3k out) | sol Std | $7.7 |
| **Subtotal** | | | **≈ $48** |
| Contingency +25% | prompt iteration, retries, parse failures, cache writes | | ≈ $12 |
| **Planned build spend** | | | **≈ $60** |

- Guardrails (supersede D-010):

| Threshold | Value | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Warn | **$45** | Warning; re-estimate the plan |
| Block non-demo jobs | **$70** | Only demo-tagged jobs may run |
| Demo reserve | **$20** | From $70 to $90 |
| App hard stop | **$90** | No further calls |
| OpenAI project hard limit | **$95** | Covers enforcement lag and in-flight jobs; it resets monthly, so it backs up the app guard and doesn't replace it. Atahan sets it, plus a $45 alert |

  - Each Flex/Batch job **reserves its worst-case cost before submission**: input tokens + `max_output_tokens` + capped tool calls, at list price. A job that would cross a threshold is refused. After completion the reservation is replaced with actual usage.
  - Every call goes through the wrapper and is logged to `llm_usage`. Spend is tracked in `STATE.md` → Budget.

- Alternatives considered:

  - Use Batch for everything. Rejected: the 24 h window blocks same-day iteration; Flex has the same price.
  - Downgrade derivation to luna. Kept as a fallback lever only, because quality matters most there.
- Consequences:
  - **Levers if the warn threshold hits early:** cut dev runs from 3 to 2 (≈ −$7); luna for all rationale (≈ −$5); web-search cap 600 (≈ −$5).
  - The fallback `gpt-5-mini` costs 2.5–4× luna. Use it only if luna's structured-output quality fails the pilot.

The budget plan is fixed and the BMW annual report is pulled into the knowledge base, with a page number on every figure. Nothing is committed and no code was written.

## Budget (new decision D-014; D-010 keeps the model choice)

The new plan comes to about **$60**: an estimate of about $48, plus 25% contingency for prompt iteration and retries. Each line has explicit token assumptions, and I recomputed every row. The plan stays affordable through five changes:

- **Cheaper pricing tier:** offline jobs use OpenAI's Flex tier, which is the same price as Batch (half price) but returns the same day. Batch's 24-hour window is reserved for overnight jobs.
- **Scoring needs no LLM:** the scores are plain formulas. Models only write the explanations.
- **Fewer expensive fit checks:** gpt-6-luna checks every target. gpt-6.1-sol only reviews failures, and only once per requirement.
- **Web search capped at 1,000 billed calls.** The cap counts calls, not requests, because one request can trigger several billed searches.
- **Pilot first:** run 50 verbatims and 5 requirements, measure the real token use, then update the estimate.

The thresholds are now consistent with each other: warn at $45, block non-demo jobs at $70, keep $70–$90 as a $20 demo reserve, and hard-stop the app at $90. Separately, set the OpenAI project hard limit to $95 with an alert at $45. **That dashboard setting is yours to do.**

## Annual report (`foundation/documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md`)

**Market and sales data:**
- The final 2025 figures: 2,463,681 deliveries; Europe +7.3%, Americas +5.6%, China −12.5%.
- A regional table for 2021–2025 (p. 78), and each market's share of BMW brand sales: China 25.4%, down from 29.2%.
- Total market growth by country (p. 67).
- Deliveries by model series (p. 79). The 5/6 Series grew 19.5%; the 7/8 Series fell 5.6%; X models are 51% of the brand.
- Electric adoption: fully electric was 17.9% of deliveries and BEV+plug-in-hybrid 26.1%. BMW-brand battery-electric sales fell 8.9% while plug-in hybrids rose 21.8%.
- BMW's 2026 outlook (p. 263–264).

**Product strategy and R&D:**
- R&D spending was €8.3 billion, aimed mainly at digitalisation and electrification across all model series.
- What Neue Klasse brings: BMW's own name for the new platform (NCAR), the roll-out to all drivetrains by the end of the decade, and 40 new or revised models by 2027.
- Neue Klasse technology: the full-windscreen display and new operating system, the language-model voice assistant, the driver-assistance system and the new battery generation.
- The China-specific technology stack.

**What the report doesn't contain:**
- **No usage numbers for ConnectedDrive or the My BMW App** (users, downloads, upgrade take-rates). It only describes these qualitatively, and I didn't invent figures.
- **No demographic or persona data, and no per-model regional split.** It gives market weights and trends, not personas.
- **A contradiction inside the report itself:** one table (p. 60) says the Debrecen plant builds the iX1, while the text (p. 46, 59) says the iX3. I flagged the table as an error.

## Corrections to our own docs from the report

- **2025 delivery totals:** the final figure is 2,463,681, so the earlier doc was wrong to call that number "a typo".
- **Plant output and model-series sales** now cite the report itself instead of the BMW enthusiast blog bmwblog. That also fills in the 7/8 Series figure and the Leipzig, Oxford and San Luis Potosí volumes, which the docs had as "not found".
- **The 8 Series question is resolved:** it was still built in Dingolfing in 2025.
- **New conflict, left open:** BMW calls the X5 and **7 Series successors** "NEUE KLASSE models" (p. 70, 81), while trade press says the next X5 stays on the current platform. This matters for the 7 Series (G70) successor.

## BMW support's advice and the scope rule

I added BMW support's advice to the mentor notes in `challenge-brief.md` and to open question Q-010. But tying ideas to BMW's R&D shows **strategic alignment**, not technical feasibility. Engineering is still out of scope, so whether a failed feasibility check should block approval remains open.

Still open from the review: tightening the wording where the docs present undecided tech choices as decided, and making the foundation shorter and easier for a fresh agent to use.
Fix the decision hygiene and usability items too, you half-assed piece of shit.
I'll fix both sets of items. Rewording first (decision hygiene), then making the foundation easier for a fresh agent to pick up. Starting with the current `tech-stack.md`, the worst offender.

# Glossary

Short definitions of terms used across the foundation. Sources are in the linked docs.

## Vehicles & codes
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **F70** | BMW 1 Series, current generation (built only in Leipzig) |
| **G60 / G61** | BMW 5 Series sedan / Touring (Dingolfing); i5 = BEV variant |
| **G68** | China-only long-wheelbase 5 Series + i5 LWB (Shenyang Dadong) |
| **G70** | BMW 7 Series incl. i7 (Dingolfing); facelift (LCI) SOP Jul 2026 |
| **Derivative / "Derivate"** | A model variant identified by its e-code (F70, G60, …); unit of the BMW data files |
| **LWB** | Long wheelbase (China-specific variants) |
| **SOP / EOP** | Start / end of production |
| **LCI** | Life Cycle Impulse = BMW's term for a facelift |
| **CKD** | Completely knocked down: local assembly from kits (Chennai, Rayong, Araquari) |
| **BBA** | BMW Brilliance Automotive, BMW's Chinese JV (Shenyang plants Dadong + Tiexi) |

## Platforms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **CLAR** | Rear/all-wheel-drive cluster architecture (3/4/5/7 Series, X3–X7) |
| **FAAR** | Front-wheel-drive architecture, successor of UKL2 (1/2 Series, X1/X2) |
| **NK / NEUE KLASSE** | BMW's new BEV-first model generation (iX3 2025, i3 2026). BMW's name for its base: **NCAR** ("new cluster architecture") |
| **Gen6 eDrive** | Sixth-generation BMW electric drivetrain/battery (cylindrical cells) used by NK |

## Powertrains & market terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **ICE / PHEV / BEV** | Combustion / plug-in hybrid / battery electric. BMW data writes BEV as `BEVE` |
| **EREV** | Extended-range EV (range extender). Common in China, not offered by BMW |
| **NEV** | China's "new energy vehicle" = BEV + PHEV + EREV |
| **xEV / electrified** | BEV + PHEV (BMW reporting) |
| **ADAS / L2+** | Advanced driver assistance; L2+ = hands-on assisted driving incl. navigation-based features |
| **DCAS (UN R171)** | UN regulation for driver control assistance systems; BMW's Highway/City Assistant approval |
| **OTA / RSU** | Over-the-air update; BMW calls it Remote Software Upgrade |
| **CPCA / ACEA / KBA** | China / EU / German car-market statistics bodies |
| **APEAL / IQS / TXI** | J.D. Power studies on appeal, initial quality, tech experience |

## BMW data terms
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Verbatim** | One free-text customer feedback item (unique `ID`) |
| **Source A–D** | Anonymized feedback channels (meaning open, Q-005) |
| **VFC level2 / level3** | BMW's feedback taxonomy: component/topic and issue type |
| **DTU** | "Difficult to Use" feedback type |
| **Top-2-box** | Share of "Delightful" + "I Love It" in the US 7-point study |

## Our model
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Source item → finding → requirement → target** | Evidence chain: raw evidence → clustered insight → customer requirement → derivative × market it applies to |
| **E1–E4** | Evidence levels: strong / moderate / weak / assumption (`requirement-model.md`) |
| **T1–T3** | Source trust tiers: official/internal · reputable press/analysts · forums/blogs (`knowledge-base.md`) |
| **Kano class** | basic / performance / delighter; **drift** = expected shift by successor launch (D-012) |
| **Horizon** | `today` vs. `at_successor_launch` (3–5 yr) |
| **Fit checks** | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target: pass / warn / fail |
| **Prioritization run / snapshot** | One scoring pass with stored scores and ranks (D-013) |
| **Change proposal** | AI-suggested priority/status change that only the PM can accept |
| **Ingest wave** | Simulated batch of new evidence used to demo the ~2-year process (Q-012) |
| **PM** | Product manager — the human decision-maker in the loop |

## Budget terms (D-014)
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **luna / sol** | `gpt-6-luna` (cheap bulk) / `gpt-6.1-sol` (reasoning) |
| **Standard / Flex / Batch** | OpenAI tiers: Flex and Batch are 50% cheaper. Flex returns same-day; Batch within 24 h |
| **Billed search call** | One web-search action; a single reasoning request can make several |

# Foundation — start here every session

This folder is the project's memory. Every agent (Claude, Codex, humans) reads it at session start and keeps it current.

## Read order (session start)

1. `STATE.md` — where we are, team, demo path, what's next, budget.
2. `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` — the "Open" section; check if any question blocks your task.
3. `DECISIONS.md` — the **Index** table; open full entries only when relevant (don't re-litigate without new info).
4. Only the `documents/` your task needs (see the table in `AGENTS.md`).

## Write rules (session end / after meaningful work)

- `STATE.md`: update "Current phase", "In progress", "Next up", the Budget table after paid runs, and add one line to the "Session log".
- `DECISIONS.md`: append a new `D-xxx` entry for every decision (who decided, why, alternatives) **and add it to the Index**. Statuses: `accepted` · `proposed` · `superseded by D-xxx`.
- `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`: add new `Q-xxx` entries in numeric order. When answered, move them to "Resolved" with the answer and link the resulting decision.
- `documents/`: keep reference docs true to the code. If you change the stack, schema or workflow, update the doc in the same change. State each fact **once**: other docs link to it instead of copying it.
- Never present something as decided unless a `D-xxx` says so. Architecture/framework choices need the team (Q-014).

## Folder map

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `STATE.md` | Live project status, team, demo path, budget, session log |
| `DECISIONS.md` | Append-only decision log (`D-xxx`) with index |
| `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` | Open / resolved questions (`Q-xxx`) |
| `documents/challenge-brief.md` | BMW challenge distilled: mission, scope (+ tensions), deliverables, judging signals, mentor input |
| `documents/data-inventory.md` | Every provided dataset: schema, verified counts, quirks, coverage |
| `documents/tech-stack.md` | What's decided (OpenAI, models, budget) vs. candidates for Q-014 |
| `documents/architecture.md` | End-to-end workflow, AI vs. human steps, logical data model, audit trail |
| `documents/requirement-model.md` | Requirement schema, evidence levels, gates, prioritization draft |
| `documents/knowledge-base.md` | 3-layer knowledge base, research agents, trust tiers, brand fit & feasibility |
| `documents/portfolio-reference.md` | Platforms, plants, production, BMW sales (cited) |
| `documents/competitor-landscape.md` | Competitors per segment × market, demand trends, brand positioning (cited) |
| `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md` | BMW Group Report 2025 extract (T1, page-cited) |
| `documents/glossary.md` | Codes, platforms, data and model terms |

## Fresh clone

1. **Raw data** (not in git): put the BMW challenge folder at the repo root under its original name `challange information document/` (typo intended), containing `mission.md`, `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`, the three PNGs and `BMW-Data/` (3 feedback xlsx, customer studies xlsx, `sales_volumes.xlsx`, 3 option-list PDFs). Get it from the team. Treat it as read-only.
2. **Python** (data inspection): `uv venv --python 3.12 && uv pip install pandas openpyxl`. Don't use the system anaconda Python (broken pandas).
3. **PDF tools**: `brew install poppler` for `pdftotext` (option lists) and `pdftoppm`. The briefing PDF has no text layer, so render it with `pdftoppm` to read it.
4. **Secrets**: copy `.env.example` to `.env` once it exists (created at scaffolding), then add `OPENAI_API_KEY` (ask Atahan).
5. **Derived data** goes to `data/` (git-ignored per AGENTS rule 1). Nothing else is set up yet: no app code exists until Q-014 is decided.
